steps.title: Prepare S277 host pre‑culture
steps.instruction: In a sterile 50 mL tube add 50 mL MRS broth, inoculate with ~100 µL frozen Oenococcus oeni S277 culture, and incubate statically for 5 days at 25 °C.

steps.title: Infect S277 and recover lysate
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of the pre‑culture and dilute to obtain three 50 mL cultures at OD₆₀₀ = 0.1 (~10⁸ CFU/mL) in sterile 250 mL bottles using MRSΦ broth; add OE33PA phage to two cultures to reach MOI = 1 (e.g., 25 µL of 10⁹ PFU/mL phage to 50 mL culture); leave the third as uninfected control; incubate 48 h statically at 25 °C; confirm lysis (infected OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.05 vs control ≈ 1); centrifuge lysed cultures at 10 000 × g for 10 min at 10 °C; transfer supernatants to a 50 mL syringe, filter through a 0.22 µm PES membrane into a sterile 100 mL bottle and pool the two filtered lysates.

steps.title: Titrate lysate by double‑layer method
steps.instruction: Prepare ten‑fold serial dilutions of the pooled lysate down to 10⁻⁷ in 1 mL 1× ΦB using 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes (store at 4 °C if needed); heat two tubes containing 5 mL MRSΦ soft agar, then cool to ~55 °C (supercooled); take two solid MRS plates, divide one into 8 equal quadrants; prepare 1 mL fresh S277 culture at OD₆₀₀ = 0.2; inoculate 0.2 mL of this culture into each soft‑agar tube, homogenize and quickly pour each onto a plate, allowing it to solidify while still supercooled; spot 0.008 mL of each dilution (undiluted to 10⁻⁷) onto the quadranted plate squares and let air‑dry under sterile conditions (second plate serves as negative control); incubate plates 4–5 days at 25 °C; count plaques at the lowest dilution and calculate titer using N = Σ P v d (P = plaques, v = 0.008 mL, d = dilution factor).

steps.title: Concentrate phage particles
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the remaining lysate in two sterile 50 mL centrifuge tubes at 20 000 × g for 2 h at 4 °C; discard supernatant and dry the pellets; gently resuspend each pellet in 5 mL sterile 1× ΦB (store at 4 °C for a few days). The suspension should reach ≥10⁹ PFU/mL; if not, proceed to the alternative low‑titer protocol.

steps.title: Purify phage via dialysis
steps.instruction: Fill a suitable container (e.g., 2 L beaker) with 1.2 L 1× ΦB, place on a magnetic stirrer and insert a rod magnet; transfer the two 5 mL phage suspensions into the Float‑A‑Lyzer® G2 (100 kDa) and close with its screw cap; enclose the Float‑A‑Lyzer® in its float and immerse in the buffer with gentle agitation for 1.5–2 h at room temperature; replace the buffer every 1.5–2 h (typically two renewals) until the phage suspension becomes colorless; move the phage suspension aseptically to a new 50 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 20 000 × g for 2 h at 4 °C; discard supernatant, air‑dry the pellet while the tube remains horizontal; resuspend the pellet in the desired volume of 1× ΦB (10–50 µL) to obtain the final concentration; store at 4 °C for a few weeks.

steps.title: Alternative low‑titer lysate protocol
steps.instruction: If the lysate titer is <10⁹ PFU/mL (e.g., 5 × 10⁷ PFU/mL), produce a larger volume (e.g., 2000 mL) of lysate; centrifuge the increased volume as in the concentration step, adjusting tube numbers accordingly; resuspend all pellets in sterile 1× ΦB to obtain a total of ~10 mL phage suspension; then continue with the purification steps described above.

steps.title: Prepare negatively stained EM grids
steps.instruction: Glow‑discharge 300‑mesh carbon‑coated copper grids (carbon side up) for 1 min at 30 mA; apply 6 µL phage sample to the carbon side for 30 s, then side‑blot excess with filter paper; briefly touch the grid to a 10 µL droplet of 1 % uranyl acetate, blot, then stain with a fresh 10 µL droplet of 1 % uranyl acetate for 10 s and blot dry; load the grid into a TEM operating at 120 kV, perform alignments, and acquire images with a CCD camera using an electron dose of 20 e⁻/Å² at the desired magnification.
